note: Re-check of the Oct 30 finding that no Adobe page documents Content Analytics with the other products of the Omnichannel Content Activation play, plus Edge Delivery Services. Five researchers (Oct 31, Claude Code workflow), one per pair, each asked to find what the first search missed. None found a documented connection, so no verifier ran. Quotes were checked against downloaded pages unless marked otherwise.

not_documented.searched: Still no. A much wider sweep than the Oct 30 search found no Adobe page that describes Content Analytics and AEM Sites working together, so for this pair it was not an oversight. Content Analytics measures every website the same way: it goes on the site through a Tags property with the Adobe Content Analytics extension, or through its JavaScript library on top of Web SDK; its featurization service then reads each page by its URL (crawler user agent AdobeFeaturization/1.0); and the reports run inside Customer Journey Analytics. An AEM Sites site can be measured that way like any other site, and Adobe's own Content Analytics webinar says it 'works with any CMS or digital asset management platform'. But neither product's documentation names the other. Coverage: all 451 pages of the CJA guide (24 mention Content Analytics, none mention Experience Manager or AEM); all 10 Content Analytics pages, including the Standalone configuration page (updated Oct 16 2026), which the Oct 30 trail did not list; all 1,447 pages of the AEM as a Cloud Service guide (no 'Content Analytics', no featurization crawler, and no Customer Journey Analytics product mention); the 45 Sites Optimizer pages (built on Operational Telemetry, no analytics product named); the 151 AEM Learn Sites tutorials; all 268 aem.live pages; and Adobe's 54-page Experience Cloud integrations guide. That guide's integration pairs give AEM Acrobat Sign, Analytics, Campaign, Commerce, Marketo Engage, Target and Workfront, and give CJA Real-Time CDP and Analytics, with no Content Analytics pair. The closest page is Coworker's 'Plan a digital campaign launch'. In one Coworker conversation it 'reviews content analytics' and later builds an offer landing page in AEM. But it never names the Content Analytics product (its own product list says Customer Journey Analytics), the review feeds the Journey Optimizer email test, and nothing passes between the two products. For the canvas: keep ca-aemsites as not documented. At most, add a note that Content Analytics measures any site, AEM Sites included, citing the webinar line. My inference, not an Adobe-documented integration: a partner would follow Content Analytics' own setup on the AEM site (its Tags property or the JavaScript library, and allow-listing the AdobeFeaturization crawler), and AEM's CDN and traffic-filter docs never name that crawler. Limits: business.adobe.com could not be read directly (WebFetch got 503), so Adobe marketing pages were judged from search snippets only. Off-pair flag: the CJA product description (effective 22 Oct 2026) says that since February 2026 Content Analytics can no longer be licensed as a CJA add-on and is sold standalone.

The Oct 30 finding holds: no Adobe page describes Content Analytics and AEM Assets working together. This search went much wider than the first one:
- I re-read the whole Content Analytics guide. That is all 10 pages in its table of contents; it has no FAQ or featurization page, and those URLs return 404.
- I crawled every page of the Customer Journey Analytics (CJA) guide, 451 pages. "Experience Manager" never appears.
- I crawled the whole AEM Assets section of the AEM Cloud Service guide, 217 pages including Content Hub, Dynamic Media, Dynamic Media with OpenAPI, Content Advisor and Assets Insights. I also crawled the other 677 AEM Cloud Service pages and the 2023 to 2026 AEM release notes. "Content Analytics" and "Customer Journey Analytics" never appear in any of them.
- I also checked the CJA and Experience Cloud release notes, the helpx product descriptions, Adobe's Content Analytics security overview, the CJA tutorials, the One Adobe tutorial, Experience League webinars and their transcripts, news.adobe.com press releases and the aem.live docs index.

How the two actually relate: Content Analytics records an asset by the image URL it sees on the live site. It then fetches the public page and image again to work out the attributes. So images served from AEM Assets or Dynamic Media are measured like images from any DAM, and no data passes between the two products.

Adobe's own matrix of AEM Cloud Service integrations ticks AEM Assets only for Analytics, Commerce, Journey Optimizer and Workfront. The CJA row is empty and Content Analytics has no row. AEM Assets' own performance reporting, Assets Insights, needs an Adobe Analytics license.

The closest Adobe wording is one use-case row on the Experience Platform Meta Ads source page. It says Meta ad data feeds GenStudio / Content Analytics to correlate Meta performance with content variants created or managed in Adobe Experience Manager or GenStudio. That row states a goal, sits on a third product's page, names AEM in general rather than AEM Assets, and describes no data flow or setup between the two, so it does not meet the bar.

If Adam wants a dotted line, that sentence is the only one he can cite. The path behind it runs through other products, each step documented on its own:
1. AEM Assets Content Hub supplies images to GenStudio for Performance Marketing.
2. GenStudio activates Meta ads.
3. The Meta Ads source brings the ad data into Experience Platform.
4. Content Analytics' paid media channel analyzes it.

A likely source of the impression: Adobe's March 2023 press release on the new AEM announced attribute-level AI content insights as an AEM capability. What shipped (beta Sept 2024, generally available March 2025) is Adobe Content Analytics inside CJA, and no current page ties it back to AEM Assets.

Two side notes:
- Licensing: since February 2026, Content Analytics is sold only as a standalone product, no longer as a CJA add-on, but it is still set up inside Experience Platform and CJA.
- business.adobe.com could not be reached today (curl error, WebFetch 503), so I did not re-read the Content Analytics product page FAQ myself.

No Adobe page documents Content Analytics and Journey Optimizer working together, so the Oct 30 finding holds. This search went further than reading page by page. It covered the full source of Adobe's Journey Optimizer guide (1,320 pages, including the new v2 pages, as of Oct 29 2026), which never mentions Content Analytics. It also covered all ten live Content Analytics pages (updated as late as Oct 29 2026), which never mention Journey Optimizer or email. Content Analytics collects data from three channels only: web, mobile apps and paid media. Where the two names appear together (CJA's list of data view integrations, CJA templates, a 2024 press release, a Sept 2026 blueprint, the helpx product descriptions), they are listed side by side, with no data passing between them.

The one route that exists is indirect, and Adobe documents it only in pieces:
1. Content Analytics adds its dimensions and metrics to a CJA data view.
2. CJA can publish audiences to Experience Platform, and Adobe names "a journey in Adobe Journey Optimizer" as one use.
3. Journey Optimizer accepts a CJA audience only after it is wrapped in a segment definition.
Adobe's 2025 launch note for Content Analytics says it helps "define new audiences for activation", and the standalone product description includes 25 refreshing audiences. But no page names Journey Optimizer as the place content-based audiences go. So this is a possible route, not a documented connection, like the Commerce and B2B Edition note.

Adobe's product page lists email asset measurement as in development. I saw this only in search snippets, because business.adobe.com refused downloads. If it ships, it would be the natural bridge to Journey Optimizer emails.

One caution: experience capture needs page text that does not depend on "cookies or other personalization mechanisms". That suggests web pages personalized by Journey Optimizer may not suit experience reporting. This is my inference; Adobe doesn't name Journey Optimizer there.

For context only, not cited: Adobe's internal play guide puts Content Analytics in its own Content Effectiveness sub-play with Experimentation Accelerator, separate from the sub-plays built on Sites, Assets and Journey Optimizer.

The evidence quotes below back the negative finding and the indirect route. None of them describes the two products connecting.

There is still no documented connection. I found no Adobe page that describes Content Analytics and Experimentation Accelerator working together. No page says data passes between them, that one is set up using the other, or that a feature of one is built on the other.

How each product works, per Adobe:
- The accelerator takes in experiments only from Journey Optimizer (campaigns and journeys) and Adobe Target. Its insights come from its own AI: it turns each treatment's rendered HTML and screenshot into an embedding and compares that with how the treatment performed.
- Content Analytics has a separate featurization service. It reports in Customer Journey Analytics (CJA), which is not in the Omnichannel play.

The search:
- I scanned the full text of 2,373 Experience League pages: every page in the CJA, Journey Optimizer, Target, accelerator, CX Enterprise AI, blueprints, CJA tutorial, One Adobe tutorial and GenStudio for Performance Marketing guides. 42 pages name Content Analytics, 21 name the accelerator, and none name both. None name both Content Analytics and the Experimentation Agent either.
- Release notes (CJA, Journey Optimizer, Target and the monthly Experience Cloud notes), the video transcripts and Adobe news turned up nothing.
- The only Adobe pages that name both are the March 2025 Summit press release and the partner newsletter page. Both describe the two products in separate items.
- Four pages the Oct 30 search had not listed add nothing: Content Analytics standalone configuration, and the accelerator's Data usage in AI, Target integration and metrics pages.

One possible route, not documented:
- Content Analytics adds its metrics (Asset Views, Asset Clicks, Experience Views, Experience Clicks) to the CJA data views it is configured on.
- The accelerator can import a CJA metric as an experiment's primary metric when CJA is the reporting source in Target or Journey Optimizer, and a Target A/B activity can pick a CJA metric from a data view.
- So a Target test reported through the same data view might use a Content Analytics metric. No Adobe page says this, Target is not in the Omnichannel play, and Journey Optimizer's experiment reporting datasets must include the Proposition Interactions field group. Treat this route as unconfirmed until it is tested in a sandbox or Adobe confirms it.

The evidence quotes below do not show a connection. They show what each product takes in and the pieces of the undocumented route.

What I could not read: business.adobe.com, helpx.adobe.com and adobe.com legal PDFs were blocked from here (503 and 403 errors). Search snippets of the accelerator product page and FAQ, and of both helpx product descriptions, show no mention of the other product.

No Adobe documentation page describes Content Analytics and AEM Sites on Edge Delivery Services working together, so the Oct 30 verdict still holds for documentation. I re-read all 10 live pages of the Content Analytics guide, the CJA release notes and the Content Analytics extension release notes. I also ran a full-text search of the GitHub sources behind 16 Experience League doc sets (about 10,700 pages) and all 251 aem.live pages. None of them ties the two products together.

The earlier search did miss one real connection, but it lives in code, not in a document. Adobe's own Content Analytics JavaScript library is the library Experience League documents for setups without Tags. Its source is at github.com/adobe/content-analytics, and it ships as @adobe/content-analytics 1.0.53 and on Adobe's CDN. The library looks for Edge Delivery's window.hlx object. When Edge Delivery's experimentation plugin serves an A/B test, audience or campaign variant, the library records that variant's page as the Content Analytics experience. It reads the plugin's servedExperience value and strips Edge Delivery's .plain.html suffix. The result: content on Edge Delivery test variants is credited to the variant the visitor actually saw. The Tags extension most likely carries the same code, because it has the same 1.0.53 version and the same fixes, but I could not confirm that.

Adobe describes none of this on any page. The experimentation plugin's README lists Adobe Analytics, Target, AJO, GTM and Tealium as integrations, not Content Analytics. Edge Delivery's experiment pages say results come from Operational Telemetry.

The documented pieces do fit together. Edge Delivery's martech plugin creates a Web SDK instance named alloy, and alloy is the name the Content Analytics docs require. A partner could therefore run Content Analytics on an Edge Delivery site, but no Adobe page describes that pairing.

One lead I could not check: business.adobe.com's AEM Sites "Content insights" page reportedly offers insights at the attribute, page and asset level from AI/ML, shown next to Edge Delivery testing. That matches what Content Analytics does. business.adobe.com is blocked here, so Adam should open it and see whether it names Content Analytics. If it does, that product page would count as documentation.

aemsites: Plan a Digital Campaign Launch with Coworker (Experience League), https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/coworker/content/chat/use-cases/workflow-and-planning/plan-digital-campaign-launch : the closest page. One Coworker conversation 'reviews content analytics' and later 'builds the offer landing page in Adobe Experience Manager'. Not an integration: 'content analytics' is lowercase and the product is never named (the page's own product list says Customer Journey Analytics); the video transcript shows the review feeds the Journey Optimizer email test ('Before we create the email...'); the AEM page is a separate later step; and Coworker, a third product, does both. No data passes between Content Analytics and AEM Sites.

Meta Ads Source Overview (Experience Platform), https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-platform/sources/connectors/advertising/meta-ads : the only Experience League page found that names both Content Analytics and Adobe Experience Manager. It covers Meta ad performance data feeding GenStudio / Content Analytics to compare ad creatives 'created or managed in Adobe Experience Manager or GenStudio'. That is AEM as a source of ad content (closer to AEM Assets), not AEM Sites pages, and no data moves between Content Analytics and AEM. None of the other 13 advertising source pages names both.

Accelerate Data Insights with Coworker, AEM and CJA (Experience League), https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/coworker/content/chat/use-cases/data-insights/intelligent-implementation-and-administration/accelerate-data-insights : a video page where Coworker sets up Web SDK data collection on an AEM site (WKND) into Customer Journey Analytics. It is AEM + CJA; Content Analytics is never mentioned.

Integrate AEM Sites and Experience Platform Web SDK (AEM Learn), https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-manager-learn/sites/integrations/experience-platform/web-sdk : AEM Sites' documented path into Experience Platform, called 'foundational' for CJA and other products. Content Analytics also runs on Web SDK, but this page never names it; it is generic plumbing shared by every Web SDK product.

Getting Started with Adobe Content Analytics (Experience League on-demand webinar), https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/events/cx-analytics-ondemand-webinars/adobe-content-analytics : the Adobe presenter says Content Analytics 'works with any CMS or digital asset management platform'. It confirms AEM Sites works like any other site, but it is a CMS-agnostic statement, not an AEM Sites integration.

Generative AI in CX Enterprise Applications (Experience League), https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/cx-enterprise-ai/experience-cloud-ai/overview/generative-ai : lists Content Analytics (AI-assigned asset attributes) and AEM Sites features (Generate Variations, Sites Optimizer) in separate sections. Both are named, with no connection.

AEM Sites 'Testing and Optimisation' marketing page, https://business.adobe.com/sg/products/experience-manager/sites/testing-optimization.html (search snippets only; business.adobe.com returned 503; the search tool dates it about three years old): its Content insights section says AI/ML services break each experience into content elements and attributes. That sounds like Content Analytics, but the page never names it and predates the product's March 27 2025 release (CJA 2025 release notes).

AEM Sites 'Content Insights' marketing page titled 'Content analytics improve your insights', https://business.adobe.com/uk/products/experience-manager/sites/content-insights.html (snippet only): a name collision. It is AEM's Content Insights page reporting fed by Adobe Analytics (Experience League documents Content Insight only for AEM 6.5), not the Adobe Content Analytics product.

An older AEM Sites marketing page on business.adobe.com (about 2023; snippet only; exact URL not confirmed) pairs AEM Sites with Customer Journey Analytics: 'Understand and measure the characteristics of experiences that resonate with your customers to optimize content creation for any audience segment.' It names CJA, not Content Analytics, and describes no mechanism.

Adobe CX Analytics Catalog Pricing Guide, https://business.adobe.com/products/adobe-analytics/pricing.html (snippet only): lists 'Adobe Experience Manager (AEM) Assets' among Content Analytics data sources, with no AEM Sites entry. Not this pair, but worth re-checking for the ca-aemassets pair, which was also marked not documented.

AEM Assets Insights and Content Hub Asset Insights (AEM as a Cloud Service guide): asset performance from Adobe Analytics and Content Hub usage, not Content Analytics; and they are AEM Assets features, not AEM Sites.

One Adobe tutorial, GenStudio Labs (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/platform-learn/tutorial-one-adobe/genstudiocsc, Oct 16 2026): lists AEM Assets modules under Asset Management and a Content Analytics module under Reporting & Insights in the same learning path. Experience League webinars, transcripts on video.tv.adobe.com: 'Roadmap to Value with Content Supply Chain - Use Cases' (2026, https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/events/adobe-customer-success-webinar-recordings/2026/aem2026/value-with-content-supply-chain) groups 'Gen Studio for performance marketing, work front, AM assets, content analytics' under remixing and optimizing content for performance. Both are suite-level groupings with no data flow or setup.
